objectives: Explain Isaac's charge to Jacob not to take a wife of Canaan.
Contrast Jacob's obedience with Esau's response.
Explain the weight of Jacob's vow at Bethel.
takeaways: The fathers from the beginning married wives of their own kindred and were blessed in their children (Tobit 4:12).
With the charge came the blessing of Abraham: fruitful, multiplied, and heir to the land.
Esau answered his father's grief by doing his own thing; the wicked hate instruction (Psalms 50:16-17).
Jacob vowed that the Lord would be his God and he would give the tenth, and he paid his vow.
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it (Ecclesiastes 5:4-6).
